title: Basic Java Program

title: Print Without a Line Break

title: Comment Types
objective: Use all three Java comment styles in one program and confirm that none of them appear in the output.
description:
Task: Write a Java program that uses all three kinds of Java comments:
- A documentation comment (/** ... */) directly above the class declaration.
- A block comment (/* ... */) inside the main() method.
- A single-line comment (// ...) inside the main() method.

The program must display the following three lines and nothing else:
Single-line comment added
Block comment added
Documentation comment added

Comments are ignored by the compiler, so none of the comment text should appear in the output.
output_format:
Three lines:
Single-line comment added
Block comment added
Documentation comment added
sample_output_1:
Single-line comment added
Block comment added
Documentation comment added
hint_1: A single-line comment starts with // and ends at the end of the line.
hint_2: A block comment starts with /* and ends with */; a documentation comment starts with /** and ends with */.
hint_3: Place the /** */ comment above public class Main, put the other two comments inside main(), and add three println() statements.
test_cases: [{"input": "", "output": "Single-line comment added\nBlock comment added\nDocumentation comment added", "is_hidden": false}]

title: Print Quotation Marks
objective: Use the \" escape sequence to print double quotation marks inside a String literal.
description:
Task: Write a Java program that displays the following line exactly, including the double quotation marks:
She said "Java is fun"

A double quote normally ends a String literal, so you need an escape sequence to print it.
output_format: A single line: She said "Java is fun"
hint_1: Writing "She said "Java is fun"" causes a compile error because the second quote ends the String.
hint_2: The escape sequence \" prints a double quotation mark.
hint_3: Use System.out.println("She said \"Java is fun\"");
test_cases: [{"input": "", "output": "She said \"Java is fun\"", "is_hidden": false}]

title: Print a Windows Path
objective: Use the \\ escape sequence to print a backslash character.
description:
Task: Write a Java program that displays the following Windows folder path exactly:
C:\Program Files\Java\bin

In a Java String literal, a single backslash starts an escape sequence, so you need a special sequence to print one backslash.
output_format: A single line: C:\Program Files\Java\bin
hint_1: A single \ followed by a letter is treated as an escape sequence, and \P or \J causes a compile error.
hint_2: The escape sequence \\ prints one backslash.
hint_3: Use System.out.println("C:\\Program Files\\Java\\bin");
test_cases: [{"input": "", "output": "C:\\Program Files\\Java\\bin", "is_hidden": false}]

title: Tab-Aligned Header
objective: Use the \t escape sequence to separate values with tab characters.
description:
Task: Write a Java program that displays a two-line table. Separate the values on each line with a single tab character, not spaces.

Line 1: Name, Dept, and Year
Line 2: Alex, CSE, and 2026

Each line should have exactly one tab between neighbouring values and no tab at the beginning or end.
output_format:
Two lines:
Name<TAB>Dept<TAB>Year
Alex<TAB>CSE<TAB>2026

hint_2: Spaces and tabs look similar on screen but are different characters, so the judge treats them differently.
hint_3: Use System.out.println("Name\tDept\tYear"); and a similar statement for the second line.
